lines.text: The concept is looked up as a Bar (Planning Code § 102).
Zoning district NCT-MISSION: a Bar on the first story is a conditional use (Planning Code § 754, in force from 2024-01-14 (Ord. 249-23, File No. 230701)).

NCT-MISSION: the table caps the eating and drinking uses (Restaurants, Limited Restaurants and Bars) in the district at 179, and a new one is not permitted if it would take the total above that (Table 754 Note 7, in force from 2024-01-14 (Ord. 249-23, File No. 230701)). Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: A new or relocated Bar is considered under the underlying zoning, but always as a Conditional Use. Here: a Bar is a conditional use (Planning Code § 249.60(b)(2)(C), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: A new Bar must use a liquor licence transferred from another Bar located inside the district. This is a requirement, not a control (Planning Code § 249.60(b)(2)(C), in force since before 2022-01-01).

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District: The § 202.2 operating conditions apply to every liquor establishment in the district; new, relocated or expanded ones, and any with a licence referred to Planning by ABC, must also provide outside lighting, keep window signage to 33% and keep 50% clear glazing on street-facing facades. This is a requirement, not a control (Planning Code § 249.60(d), in force since before 2022-01-01).

comparable_cases.why_comparable: This is an agency referral for the exact same address (200 Capp St) in 2019, approving continuation of the existing bar use (DBA Uptown) with a Type 48 license in the NCT-MISSION district and Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved continuation of the bar use at this location but explicitly stated no intensification or expansion would be allowed in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD without a conditional use authorization. This is an agency referral, not a Commission hearing, so it shows administrative approval but not full discretionary review.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Earlier agency referral at the same address (200 Capp St) in 2015 approving an ownership transfer of the Type 48 license for the existing bar use (DBA Uptown) per Planning Code Section 249.60(c) governing the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 48 ownership transfer at this exact location under the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD rules. Both this and the 2019 referral were continuations of an existing bar, not establishment of a new bar use, which is the critical distinction in the Special Use District.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Agency referral 195 meters away at 2901 16th St approving a Type 48 license for a restaurant/bar use. The record explicitly states the license was transferred from within the Mission Alcohol Restrict SUD (from 2950 16th Street City Club), demonstrating compliance with the district's transfer requirement.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 48 bar use in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD by confirming the license was transferred from another location already within the district, as required by Planning Code Section 249.60(c). This shows the pathway for establishing bar use in the SUD: transfer from within the district.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Second agency referral for the same 2901 16th St project (Board of Supervisors/Public Convenience or Necessity referral), 195 meters away, also noting the Type 48 license transfer from within the Mission Alcohol Restrict SUD and that it was not treated as a change of use under Planning Code Section 843.45.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The dual referrals show both Planning and ABC coordination was required. The finding that restaurant-to-bar was not a 'change of use' under Section 843.45 when the license came from within the district suggests flexibility when the SUD transfer requirement is met.

filing_playbook.action: Request a written zoning determination from SF Planning Department stating whether the concept is a continuation of the bar use that operated until February 21, 2024, or a new bar requiring a Conditional Use Authorization.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Describe the concept as Kiitos, a bar with limited kitchen at 200 Capp St, where a Type 48 license (ABC #559557, DBA Uptown) was surrendered on February 21, 2024. State the operator intends to serve alcohol (specify beer-and-wine or full liquor) and ask: (1) Is this a continuation of the prior bar use or a new bar? (2) If new, is a Conditional Use Authorization required? (3) If a CUA is required, must the Type 48 license be transferred from another bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD? Request the determination cite the applicable Planning Code sections and any rule on the 179-unit eating-and-drinking cap in NCT-MISSION.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms continuation is allowed without a CUA, or after the CUA is approved, apply for the ABC license with a signed lease, zoning sign-off, seller's permit, and entity registration.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the ABC application with a signed lease, zoning sign-off from SF Planning (either the written determination from Step 1 or the CUA approval from Step 2), a seller's permit, and the entity registration. For a Type 48, provide evidence the license is transferred from a bar already within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD if Planning requires it. For a Type 41 or 47, describe the concept as a bona fide eating place with waiter or waitress service and meals prepared on-site. Post the ABC notice at the premises for 30 days and notify the Police Department Liaison Unit and Planning Department that the application has been filed.

filing_playbook.action: File the building permit application for tenant improvements with SF Department of Building Inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit stamped plans for the kitchen hood and suppression system (if installing a new hood), ADA restroom upgrades, and any structural or mechanical work. Coordinate electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits with licensed subcontractors. Budget 14–120 days.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: If the limited kitchen uses grease (cooking oil, butter, or animal fat), register with SF Public Utilities Commission for the Fats, Oils & Grease program and install a grease interceptor before the final building inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the Installation Verification Form to SFPUC after the interceptor is installed, sized per the Discharger Category assigned by the inspector. Budget 14–45 days for SFPUC review. An undersized or missing interceptor will delay the building permit final sign-off.

filing_playbook.action: Before opening, ensure all staff complete California Food Handler cards and RBS alcohol server training, subscribe to ASCAP and BMI music licenses, and register with EDD as an employer.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Every employee handling food must obtain a Food Handler card within 30 days of hire (online, 2 hours, $7–15). Every employee serving alcohol must complete RBS training within 60 days of hire ($3 registration plus $10–25 course). Subscribe to ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for recorded music ($300–2,500 each annually). These are quick but often forgotten.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline and cost ranges cover a Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–15,000 per the catalog entry for sf.conditional_use_authorization), health permit to operate (14–45 days, $470–1,000 per catalog:sf.health_permit), health plan check (21–60 days, $828–2,500 per catalog:sf.health_plan_check), and building permit (14–120 days, $800–15,000 per catalog:sf.building_permit). These are times to approval when the approvals are granted, measured from filing to decision; they do not include time to a denial or withdrawal. The ranges assume the CUA, health plan check, and building permit are filed concurrently or in close sequence, so the overall timeline is dominated by the CUA (the longest single approval). ABC license timelines and fees are not included because the alcohol type and license-acquisition strategy are not known. If the concept is confirmed to be a continuation of the prior bar use without a CUA, the timeline drops to 35–165 days and the cost to $2,800–6,200 (health and building only). The figures are from the permit catalog entries cited and do not include construction costs, architect fees, or license transfer purchase prices.

records_summary: 200 Capp St operated as a bar (DBA Uptown) with a Type 48 full-bar license until February 21, 2024, when the license was surrendered—the same day as this report. The space sits in the Mission Street NCT district where a bar is a conditional use, and inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which requires any new bar to use a Type 48 license transferred from another bar already located within the district. The block is densely developed with food and drink businesses: 21 registered businesses within 500 feet and four active ABC on-sale licenses. The records contain no dated Planning Commission decisions for comparable bar or nightlife uses within 1,000 feet in the last ten years, so no approval rate can be shown.
